clue.text: Last queen but one between posts

parts.note: to last is to keep, as food keeps or endures
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A monarch who is the second-to-last of her line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last queen but one' reads as 'penultimate queen', but 'but' is only a link and the definition is the goalkeeper's spot between the posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper stands between the goalposts, guarding the net in football or hockey.

clue.text: Sound fish looked at with interest

indicators.note: sound here means said out loud, so the word for the fish is heard as another word

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: A healthy fish was watched closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to gaze at it with interest or desire.

clue.text: Is nosy girl one to make sacrifices?

parts.note: someone who is nosy pries into others' affairs
Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's novel

explanation.surface: A question about whether an inquisitive young woman is self-sacrificing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a girl giving things up; the definition means a woman who offers sacrifices at an altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestesses in ancient religions performed ritual sacrifices to the gods.

clue.text: Decisive defeat with terrorist group at first in poor spirits

indicators.note: in places the two opening letters inside the word for a decisive defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of each of the words terrorist and group

explanation.surface: A heavy loss and a militant faction leave people feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor spirits' looks like low morale but means cheap, harsh liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotgut is slang for cheap, low-quality alcohol, so it is literally inferior spirits.

clue.text: Fancy notepaper, nonetheless, for arrested juvenile

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, signalling these letters are rearranged
read as none-the-less: drop the O, which stands for none or nothing, from the stationery word

explanation.surface: Ornate writing paper, all the same, for a youngster in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' means stunted in development, not taken by police: the boy who never grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's hero never grows up, a byword for arrested development in a child.

clue.text: Creepy fat child's dicky birds

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or faulty, so the preceding letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A scary overweight youngster's unreliable pets.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky (shaky) also chimes with dicky-bird, a childish word for bird.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small black-and-white songbirds of Europe, a species of flycatcher.

clue.text: Deficit? Artist not quite down in the mouth

indicators.note: in a down entry, down in places the painter's shortened name inside the word for mouth

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap

indicators.note: not quite tells us to drop the last letter of the painter's name

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: Is a painter running short of money feeling glum?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down in the mouth' looks like the idiom for sad, but splits into a placing instruction and the slang word for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a shortfall when a country's imports exceed its exports.

clue.text: Erotic pose one ignored on page three, say

indicators.note: to pose is to arrange, so the letters remaining are set out in a new order
ignored means the letter standing for one is left out

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A sexy photo-shoot on a tabloid's Page Three.
explanation.walkthrough: Page Three of The Sun was notorious for topless models; here page three is just an odd-numbered page. EROTC, from Erotic less I, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of a book, which carries odd numbers such as three.

clue.text: It seems to be put on without a tear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cosmetic word wraps around the rest

parts.note: to apply something is to put it on, like paint or cream
a rent is a tear or rip in cloth

explanation.surface: Something seemingly worn while free of any rip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is a rip, not a drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is used to mean so it seems, evidently, as far as one can tell.

clue.text: Run down heartless brute with mini

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of brute, keeping only its outside pair

parts.note: mini means small or little

explanation.surface: A thug driving a small car runs someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' suggests a road accident with a Mini car; it means disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise them, making them seem small or unimportant.

clue.text: Abide by church given power in law

indicators.note: in places church and power inside the word for a law

parts.note: an act is a law passed by parliament
CE is the Church of England
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Obey a statute that grants the church authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a rule or ruling is to abide by it, submitting to it.

clue.text: Prepare to deal and get on with the game

parts.note: before dealing cards you shuffle the pack
to board is to get on a ship, bus or train

explanation.surface: Advice to a card player: mix the pack and play on.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-table surface hides a deck game played by pushing discs along a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuffleboard is a game in which players slide discs onto a scoring area.

clue.text: Unending hoo-ha

definitions.meaning: a fuss or commotion, overexcited behaviour

explanation.surface: An endless fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both continuing and, as a noun, a fuss or excited behaviour.

clue.text: Come to party after funeral

definitions.meaning: a gathering held after a burial, or a vigil beside the body

explanation.surface: An invitation to the gathering after a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake is to come round from sleep; a wake is also a post-funeral gathering.

clue.text: One from Yokohama being paid in yen

indicators.note: one from picks the single opening letter of the Japanese city

parts.note: earning is being paid wages

explanation.surface: A Japanese worker paid in his country's currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like Japanese money, in keeping with Yokohama, but is a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong desire or craving, a longing for something.

clue.text: Kelly's drinking English grape juice — there is no alternative

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so English goes inside the bushranger's name

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw, so Kelly's is Ned's
must is unfermented grape juice used in winemaking

explanation.surface: An outlaw has no choice but to drink juice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from needs must when the devil drives, means one is compelled with no other option.

clue.text: One sees many pictures of Caine and ET's cast

indicators.note: cast here means thrown into a new shape, so the actor and alien letters are rearranged

parts.note: the alien's name with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A film buff watches movies starring Michael Caine and ET's actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' poses as the film's actors but is the anagram signal on CAINE plus ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a film enthusiast who watches a great many films.

clue.text: Swede, for example, with metal one can cut

parts.note: brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: cut docks the final letter from can

explanation.surface: A Swedish person and a tool for slicing tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a person from Sweden but is the vegetable, called rutabaga in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the cabbage genus, which includes the swede, turnip and broccoli.

clue.text: Serpentine swimmers with Marylebone's last golfer

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of Marylebone

parts.note: Ernie Els is the South African golfer

explanation.surface: Swimmers in the Serpentine lake are joined by a golfer from Marylebone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is a lake in Hyde Park, London, and Marylebone a nearby district, but serpentine here just means snakelike.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snakelike fish, so they are serpentine swimmers.

clue.text: Dress for Dumbo? What's up?

parts.note: a clot is a fool, a dumbo

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the exclamation is read bottom to top

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what

explanation.surface: A question about what clothing suits the flying elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumbo is the Disney elephant, but here just means a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put clothes on them, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Folded plastic sheet is to be the deciding factor

indicators.note: folded means bent into a new form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creased piece of plastic proves decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to provide the extra weight that settles an outcome one way.

clue.text: Invigorating chapter written by Morrison

indicators.note: written by places the chapter abbreviation after the author's name

parts.note: Toni Morrison, the American Nobel-winning novelist

explanation.surface: A lively chapter from a Toni Morrison novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that restores energy or refreshes, so it invigorates.

clue.text: Car dealers ignoring southern county

indicators.note: ignoring drops the county abbreviation from the end of the traders' word

parts.note: merchants are traders or dealers
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Motor traders who shun a southern county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the usual short form of Hampshire, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is informal shortening for a Mercedes-Benz motor car.

clue.text: Those answering to M answer to men

parts.note: gents are gentlemen, men

explanation.surface: A formula for responding to men.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories, to whom spies report.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents in the Bond films report to their chief, known as M.

clue.text: Geordie area's taken back, so Labour leader waxed lyrical

indicators.note: taken back means the region's abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: Geordies are from Newcastle, in the North East, NE; the 's stands for is
thus means so, therefore
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this was set

explanation.surface: North-east voters are won back, so the Labour leader gets excited.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to speak with great enthusiasm, the same as enthused.

clue.text: Any number taken in by footballer's contemptuous expression

indicators.note: taken in by means the number letter goes inside the word for footballers

parts.note: a kicker is one who kicks, a footballer; the 's stands in for the plural
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A footballer sneers after being duped by a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knickers!' is British slang for nonsense, a scornful retort.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a dismissive British way of saying rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Authentic egg sandwiches are tempting

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the letters sit inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Genuine egg sandwiches look appetising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt or lure, so things that entice are tempting.
